about:
Nagakura Engineering Works operates from Columbus, Indiana, as the U.S. base of a company founded in 1950 in Shizuoka, Japan. The business began with research into cold forging technology and has since expanded to production sites in the United States, Vietnam, and Mexico.

The company specializes in cold forging, producing more than 30 million parts annually for automotive applications. Its portfolio includes transmission components, motor and hybrid-vehicle parts, and what it describes as the world's longest cold forged shafts at 700 millimeters. Nagakura develops its own machine specifications and applies continuous improvement (Kaizen) to its equipment.

Customers are primarily in the automotive sector, including transmission manufacturers such as ZF, for which Nagakura has supported development of new generation transmissions. Parts ship globally to automakers and tier-one suppliers.

The founder's original focus on cold forging research evolved into a philosophy of tackling parts deemed impossible to produce. The company cites its "Nagakura Spirits" — challenging convention and pursuing Kaizen — as the driver behind its ability to realize high quality, high impact products.
